signatures.description: Implement a 3D convex-hull builder that survives degenerate and near-degenerate point sets: exact orientation/incircle predicates via adaptive floating-point filters with an exact BigInt fallback, initial-simplex selection that rejects collinear and coplanar seeds, and horizon-based facet construction that handles points lying exactly on a facet plane, duplicate points and cospherical ties. Assert the output invariants on every hull: V - E + F == 2, consistent facet winding with every face normal pointing away from the interior centroid, no input point strictly outside any facet plane, and every facet non-degenerate. Run it on adversarial inputs (points on a sphere, two exactly parallel planes, all points exactly coplanar so the hull must degrade to a 2D polygon, randomly permuted duplicates) and show the exact predicate agrees with a high-precision reference on 100k near-degenerate random triples where the float filter alone would be wrong.
